# Rule thresholds

<!-- Generated by scripts/thresholds_doc.py from camber/rules/param_docs.py. Do not edit by hand:
change the registry (or the rule's constructor) and re-run the script. -->

Every tunable parameter of every built-in rule: its default (read from the rule's constructor),
its unit, a sensible range, **where the default comes from**, and how to re-tune it from your own
data. `camber rules params [RULE]` prints the same information in the terminal, with a
ready-to-paste config snippet (`--yaml` puts each basis and calibration hint beside its value as a
comment; `--json` is machine-readable).

**Changing a threshold.** Give the rule's entry in a run config `params`; only the ones you set
change, the rest keep their defaults:

```json
{"rules": [{"name": "leaking_valve", "params": {"fan_heat_f": 1.0}}]}
```

or, in a YAML config (the optional `[yaml]` extra), with the calibration recorded beside it:

```yaml
rules:
  - name: leaking_valve
    params:
      # calibrated on <site> AHU-1, 2026-03-01..03-31 (fan on, both valves closed):
      # median mixed-to-supply rise 1.0 F; scored on April-June, not on March
      fan_heat_f: 1.0
    basis:
      fan_heat_f: "calibrated on AHU-1 March 2026 (fan-on, valves closed)"
```

The optional `basis` map copies that provenance into each finding of the rule
(`metrics["param_basis"]`). How to calibrate without fooling yourself is in
[Tuning thresholds with your own data](TUNING.md).

**Basis** says where a default comes from:

- `standard: ...` -- the code cites that standard and section for the value;
- `public source: ...` -- a published, non-standard source (a PNNL Re-tuning guide chapter, a
  DOE or LBNL guide, a manufacturer convention);
- `CAMBER judgment` -- an engineering choice, usually screening-grade: re-tune it first;
- `calibrated on ...` -- fitted to the named dataset or run.

**Fixed in code** lists thresholds that are not constructor parameters yet, so you can see what
you cannot tune from a config today.

The registry is a provisional API (0.98): its shape may still change before 1.0.

## airflow_tracking

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tol_frac` | `0.2` | fraction of the airflow setpoint | 0.05 to 0.5 | CAMBER judgment |
| `min_sp` | `1e-06` | cfm (the airflow setpoint's unit) | 0.0 to 500.0 | CAMBER judgment: a divide-by-zero guard |
| `warn_pct` | `10.0` | % of active samples (setpoint above min_sp) | 2.0 to 30.0 | CAMBER judgment |
| `fault_pct` | `25.0` | % of active samples (setpoint above min_sp) | 10.0 to 60.0 | CAMBER judgment |

How to calibrate:

- `tol_frac`: On a known-good period take the 95th percentile of |flow - setpoint| / setpoint (mean_abs_rel_error summarises it) and set the tolerance just above it; flow sensors read poorly at low flow.
- `min_sp`: Raise it to the box's minimum-flow setpoint (or a small fraction of design flow) to leave out samples where the relative error of a tiny setpoint is noise.
- `warn_pct`: Read off_setpoint_pct on boxes known to be healthy; set the warn level above their spread.
- `fault_pct`: Set it well above warn_pct. *Note:* Must be at or above warn_pct.

## boiler_short_cycle

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `max_starts_per_day` | `6.0` | per day | 2.0 to 24.0 | CAMBER judgment: a generic cycling limit; the right value depends on the manufacturer's minimum cycle time (the code says to confirm it against the equipment's controls) |

How to calibrate:

- `max_starts_per_day`: Take the boiler's minimum on/off cycle time from its manual or burner control and divide the day by it with margin; or use the 95th-percentile daily starts of a known-good heating season. Coarse trends undercount starts, so the count is a floor. *Note:* Warn at this many firing starts per day, fault at twice it.

## boiler_summer_lockout

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `summer_lockout_oat_f` | `65.0` | °F | 50.0 to 80.0 | CAMBER judgment: a generic mild-climate lockout; the check itself follows PNNL Re-tuning Ch.8 (boiler lockout in summer), which gives no single value |

How to calibrate:

- `summer_lockout_oat_f`: Use the heating lockout the building's sequence of operations specifies, or the outdoor temperature above which no zone has called for heat in a known-good year of trends. Set it per climate zone: higher in a hot-desert zone, lower in a cool one. *Note:* Severity is fixed in code: warn when the boiler runs at OAT above this for >= 5 % of its running hours, fault at >= 20 %. Without an OAT point the check is not evaluated.

## chiller_approach_fouling

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cond_design_f` | `5.0` | °F | 1.0 to 10.0 | CAMBER judgment: a typical clean-tube condenser approach |
| `evap_design_f` | `4.0` | °F | 0.5 to 8.0 | CAMBER judgment: a typical clean-tube evaporator approach |

How to calibrate:

- `cond_design_f`: Use the condenser approach from the chiller's selection report or start-up log, or the median of a period just after a tube cleaning at similar load. *Note:* Severity is fixed in code on the worse leg's median / design: warn at >= 1.5x, fault at >= 2x.
- `evap_design_f`: Use the evaporator approach from the chiller's selection report or start-up log, or the median of a known-good period with correct charge and flow. *Note:* Same warn (1.5x) / fault (2x) ratios as the condenser leg.

## chiller_efficiency

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `design_kw_per_ton` | `0.85` | kW/ton | 0.4 to 1.6 | CAMBER judgment: a generic ceiling between water-cooled centrifugal (~0.5-0.6) and air-cooled (~1.0-1.2) machines; the code says to set it from the chiller schedule |

How to calibrate:

- `design_kw_per_ton`: Use the chiller schedule or manufacturer selection (kW/ton at the loads it actually runs, e.g. IPLV/NPLV points), or the median kW/ton of a known-good season after a tube cleaning. Calibrating on the period you score hides a degradation already present. *Note:* Severity is fixed in code on the median kW/ton: warn at >= 1.2x this, fault at >= 1.5x. pct_hours_inefficient counts hours above 1.15x (metric only).

## chiller_staging

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `max_starts_per_day` | `6.0` | per day | 2.0 to 24.0 | CAMBER judgment: a generic cycling limit; the right value depends on the manufacturer's minimum cycle time (the code says to confirm it against the equipment's controls) |
| `low_load_pct` | `40.0` | % of the chiller's observed peak tons | 10.0 to 70.0 | CAMBER judgment: the 'idling' cut-off for the optional load-factor metric |

How to calibrate:

- `max_starts_per_day`: Take the compressor's minimum start-to-start time (anti-recycle timer) from the chiller controls and allow margin; or use the 95th-percentile daily starts of a known-good cooling season. Coarse trends undercount starts, so the count is a floor. *Note:* Warn at this many starts per day, fault at twice it.
- `low_load_pct`: Set it near the load below which the chiller's part-load curve (from the manufacturer) turns sharply less efficient, commonly 30-40 % of capacity. *Note:* Needs CHW flow and temperatures. Severity is fixed in code: warn when >= 25 % of running hours sit below this load, fault at >= 50 %. Peak is the observed peak, not nameplate.

## chiller_staging_fleet

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `redundancy_ceiling` | `0.9` | fraction of one chiller's capacity | 0.5 to 1.0 | CAMBER judgment: how fully one chiller can be loaded before the next must stage on |

How to calibrate:

- `redundancy_ceiling`: Use the plant's stage-up load from its staging sequence (e.g. 0.85-0.95 of capacity). Capacity is each chiller's 95th-percentile power, so a plant that never reaches full load reads a low capacity; lower this if the flagged hours look like correct staging. *Note:* Severity is fixed in code: warn when >= 20 % of multi-chiller hours are over-staged, fault at >= 50 %.

## chw_plant_reset

No tunable parameters.

Fixed in code: fault when >= 50 % of running hours have loop delta-T below 8 °F (the PNNL Re-tuning Ch.8 low-delta-T threshold, per camber/chwplant.py); warn at >= 20 %, or when CHWST vs OAT is flat (|slope| < 0.05 °F/°F); occupied hours only; without a run status or power, running means CHWST in 38-58 °F; CHWST <= 46 °F is reported as held low (metric only); fixed in code (camber/rules/chwplant_rule.py, camber/chwplant.py), not yet a constructor parameter

## chw_pump_dp_reset

No tunable parameters.

Fixed in code: fault when the pump runs near full speed (>= 90 % speed) for >= 60 % of its running time; warn at >= 30 % near full, or near minimum (<= 25 % speed) for >= 50 %; running means speed > 5 %; a DP setpoint with a standard deviation under 0.5 (its own units) counts as flat (no reset, reported but not in severity); fixed in code (camber/rules/chwpump_rule.py, camber/chwpump.py), not yet a constructor parameter

## chw_supply_tracking

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `above_f` | `3.0` | °F | 1.0 to 8.0 | CAMBER judgment: outside a healthy loop's ~1 °F control band, ~0.5 °F sensor accuracy and hourly staging transients together |
| `warn_pct` | `10.0` | % of running samples | 1.0 to 50.0 | CAMBER judgment |
| `fault_pct` | `25.0` | % of running samples | 5.0 to 80.0 | CAMBER judgment |
| `settle_intervals` | `1` | count (trend intervals) | 0 to 12 | CAMBER judgment: the first interval after each start is pull-down, not tracking |
| `min_running` | `24` | count (running samples) | 6 to 500 | CAMBER judgment: a day of hourly samples before judging |

How to calibrate:

- `above_f`: In a known-good period with the chiller running, take the 95th or 99th percentile of CHWST minus its setpoint and set this just above it. Do not tune it on the period you are scoring: a plant that never makes setpoint would set its own excuse.
- `warn_pct`: Look at the share of running time above setpoint + above_f on a healthy plant and set the warn well above it; a summer design-day peak can briefly exceed capacity. *Note:* Must be below fault_pct.
- `fault_pct`: Set it at a share of running time you would dispatch a technician for; keep it above warn_pct. The rule caps at warn when runtime was inferred from temperature.
- `settle_intervals`: Measure how long CHWST takes to reach setpoint after a start in trends, and divide by the trend interval (round up). With 15-minute trends this is often 2-4. *Note:* Applies only when a run status or power gate is available.
- `min_running`: Raise it for a short-sample trend (e.g. 96 for a day of 15-minute data) so the rule judges at least a day of running time.

## co2_ventilation

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `exclude_economizer` | `true` | flag | `false`, `true` | CAMBER judgment: economizer outdoor air is free cooling, not over-ventilation (0.93, #38) |
| `oa_damper_min_pct` | `null` | % open (OA damper position) | 0.0 to 60.0 | CAMBER judgment: None derives the minimum from the damper's own trend |
| `econ_high_limit_f` | `75.0` | °F (outdoor air temperature) | 55.0 to 80.0 | standard: ASHRAE 90.1 -- the top of its fixed dry-bulb economizer high-limit range, as the code cites it (no section cited) |

How to calibrate:

- `exclude_economizer`: Leave it on wherever the unit economizes. Turn it off only to see the all-hours over-ventilation share, which is also reported as over_vent_all_pct when it is on. *Note:* Affects only the over-ventilation verdict; under-ventilation is judged on every occupied hour either way. It has no effect on a frame with no ECON_CMD and no OAT with an OA damper or mixed/return temperatures.
- `oa_damper_min_pct`: Set it to the minimum-OA damper position from the BAS sequence or the TAB report. To read it from trends, take the 5th percentile of the damper while the fan runs and the damper is open, over a known-good period with no economizing (hot or cold weather). *Note:* None: the 5th percentile of the damper while open (and the fan on, when trended). An hour counts as economizing only when the damper sits more than 5 points above this minimum and the OAT is below econ_high_limit_f. Used only without an ECON_CMD point.
- `econ_high_limit_f`: Set it to the high-limit setpoint programmed in the economizer sequence. From trends, take the highest OAT at which the OA damper still opens beyond its minimum over a summer of known-good operation. *Note:* Used only when economizer mode is inferred from OAT and the damper; a trended ECON_CMD overrides it. A lower value counts fewer hours as economizing.

Fixed in code: under-ventilated when CO2 is > 700 ppm above outdoor, over-ventilated when < 150 ppm above (camber/iaq.py); fault when under-ventilated >= 20 % of occupied hours, warn at >= 5 %, or when over-ventilated >= 60 % (camber/rules/iaq_rule.py); the occupied schedule is the fixed weekday 07:00-18:00

## co2_ventilation_system

Its parameters are passed through to [`co2_ventilation`](#co2_ventilation); set them on this rule's own entry.

## cohort_airflow

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `k` | `3.5` | - (robust z, MAD-scaled) | 2.0 to 6.0 | CAMBER judgment: the common 3.5 modified-z outlier cutoff (not cited in the cohort code) |
| `min_cohort` | `3` | count | 3 to 50 | CAMBER judgment: a median and MAD need at least three peers |
| `summary` | `"mean"` | choice | `"mean"`, `"peak"`, `"load_factor"` | CAMBER judgment: the mean is the most stable summary |

How to calibrate:

- `k`: Run it on a cohort you believe healthy and read the largest |z|; set k above it. Lower k finds more outliers but flags normal spread in small cohorts.
- `min_cohort`: Raise it when the cohort mixes unlike units; small cohorts give unstable z-scores.
- `summary`: Use peak to compare maxima (sizing), load_factor (mean / peak) to compare how units cycle.

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| `min_cohort` | `3` | count | 3 to 50 | CAMBER judgment: a median and MAD need at least three peers |

How to calibrate:

- `k`: Run it on a cohort you believe healthy and read the largest |z|; set k above it. Lower k finds more outliers but flags normal spread in small cohorts.
- `min_cohort`: Raise it when the cohort mixes unlike units; small cohorts give unstable z-scores.
- `summary`: Use peak to compare maxima (sizing), load_factor (mean / peak) to compare how units cycle.

## compressor_short_cycle

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `max_starts_per_day` | `12.0` | compressor starts per day (off-to-on transitions over the trend's span) | 6.0 to 72.0 | CAMBER judgment: a generous ceiling for a DX compressor with a minimum off-time of about 5 min (the rule module's comment) |

How to calibrate:

- `max_starts_per_day`: Take the manufacturer's minimum on/off timers and the unit's staging hysteresis; better, count the starts per day in a known-good week of similar weather and set the ceiling somewhat above its highest day. Calibrating on the period you are scoring would hide a short-cycling fault. *Note:* Warn at the ceiling, fault at twice it. The span includes days the unit is off, so a trend with long idle stretches lowers the rate.

Fixed in code: warn at max_starts_per_day or more; fault at twice it (the factor 2 is fixed in code)

## compressor_staging

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `max_changes_per_day` | `24.0` | compressor-stage changes per day | 8.0 to 96.0 | CAMBER judgment: depends on the staging hysteresis; no source is cited |

How to calibrate:

- `max_changes_per_day`: Count the stage changes per day in a known-good period with a similar load and set the ceiling above its busiest day; the controller's stage-up / stage-down delays bound what a stable sequence can do. *Note:* Warn at the ceiling, fault at twice it.

Fixed in code: warn at max_changes_per_day or more; fault at twice it (the factor 2 is fixed in code)

## condenser_bypass_leak

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `closed_pct` | `2.0` | % valve command | 0.0 to 10.0 | CAMBER judgment: a command at or below this is 'shut' |
| `warn_f` | `2.0` | °F | 1.0 to 5.0 | CAMBER judgment: twice the combined ±0.5 °F accuracy of two plant sensors (screening-grade) |
| `fault_f` | `5.0` | °F | 2.0 to 15.0 | CAMBER judgment: roughly a 5-8 % rise in chiller kW/ton (screening-grade) |
| `min_samples` | `24` | count (samples) | 6 to 500 | CAMBER judgment: a day of hourly samples before judging |

How to calibrate:

- `closed_pct`: Set it to the bypass command the controller writes when fully closed, plus a little for analog noise; a controller that parks at a few percent needs a higher value.
- `warn_f`: Compare the two sensors in a known-good period with the bypass shut (e.g. after a valve rebuild) and set this above their median difference plus the sensors' combined accuracy. *Note:* It also gates both sensor-offset tests (a difference of at least +warn_f or -warn_f).
- `fault_f`: Set it at the entering-water rise worth a valve repair on this plant, from the chillers' kW/ton sensitivity to condenser-water temperature (often 1-2 % per °F). *Note:* Must be above warn_f.
- `min_samples`: Raise it for short-interval trends (e.g. 96 for a day of 15-minute data) or when the bypass is rarely shut while a chiller runs. *Note:* Also the minimum count for the bypassed-fraction estimate and the offset regression.

## condenser_water_reset

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `reset_slope_flat` | `0.3` | °F CW supply per °F wet-bulb | 0.05 to 0.8 | CAMBER judgment: an ideal reset tracks wet-bulb about 1:1, so below this it is effectively flat |

How to calibrate:

- `reset_slope_flat`: Check the reset schedule in the sequence of operations: a reset limited by a minimum condenser-water temperature has a lower slope over the year; fit the slope over a known-good period with the reset working and set this well below it. *Note:* No reset is reported as warn (an efficiency opportunity), never fault. The wet-bulb derived from OAT + RH is at sea level here.

## control_hunting

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `warn_per_hr` | `6.0` | per hour (direction reversals) | 2.0 to 20.0 | CAMBER judgment |
| `fault_per_hr` | `12.0` | per hour (direction reversals) | 4.0 to 40.0 | CAMBER judgment |
| `deadband` | `5.0` | % of stroke | 1.0 to 20.0 | CAMBER judgment: ignores slow, legitimate modulation |
| `gap_factor` | `3.0` | - (multiple of the median sample interval) | 1.5 to 10.0 | CAMBER judgment |

How to calibrate:

- `warn_per_hr`: Read reversals_per_hr on loops known to be stable (1-5 min data) and set the warn level above their spread; the trend must resolve it (max_resolvable_per_hr).
- `fault_per_hr`: Set it well above warn_per_hr, at the reversal rate where the controlled variable visibly oscillates. *Note:* Must be at or above warn_per_hr; a trend too coarse to resolve it caps severity at warn.
- `deadband`: Set it above the output's normal step size on a stable loop (the median absolute sample-to-sample move) so that small corrections are not counted as reversals.
- `gap_factor`: Raise it for a change-of-value trend whose intervals vary widely; lower it when logger outages are short but real.

## cooling_tower_approach

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `design_approach_f` | `7.0` | °F | 2.0 to 15.0 | CAMBER judgment: a well-sized, clean tower achieves ~3-7 °F; the code says to set it from the tower schedule |
| `min_effort_pct` | `90.0` | % tower fan speed | 50.0 to 100.0 | CAMBER judgment: a tower's capability is its approach at full fan (CTI rating practice); at part fan the approach is the controller's choice |
| `elevation_ft` | `null` | ft | -300.0 to 10000.0 | CAMBER judgment: None assumes sea level; a site input, not a threshold |
| `pressure_psia` | `null` | psia | 10.0 to 15.5 | CAMBER judgment: None assumes sea level; a site input, not a threshold |

How to calibrate:

- `design_approach_f`: Use the design approach from the tower selection (leaving water minus design wet-bulb). Without one, the median approach at high fan in a known-good period is a calibration, not a design value; a fouled tower calibrated this way will look healthy. *Note:* Severity is fixed in code on the median approach: warn at >= 1.3x this, fault at >= 1.7x. pct_hours_high_approach counts hours above design + 3 °F (metric only).
- `min_effort_pct`: Set it just below the fan speed the tower reaches on a hot afternoon. If the rule declines because the fan never reaches it, lower it, knowing part-fan hours judge control, not the tower. *Note:* None restores the old 'fan running' gate, which judged cold-weather hours held above a minimum condenser-water temperature. Used only when a fan speed is trended.
- `elevation_ft`: Enter the site elevation above sea level from a survey or map. It corrects a wet-bulb derived from OAT + RH; a measured wet-bulb point ignores it. *Note:* None = sea-level Stull wet-bulb, which reads high at altitude and so understates the approach. pressure_psia takes precedence when both are given.
- `pressure_psia`: Enter a typical measured barometric pressure (absolute, not sea-level corrected) at the site, or leave None and give elevation_ft. *Note:* None = use elevation_ft, or sea level when that is also None.

## damper_census

No tunable parameters.

Fixed in code: a box is throttling when its median occupied damper is < 50 % and starved when >= 90 %; fault when >= 60 % of boxes throttle or >= 25 % are starved, warn when < 50 % of boxes lie in band; occupied hours are the weekday 07:00-18:00 schedule; fixed in code (camber/rules/static_rule.py, camber/staticpressure.py), not yet a constructor parameter

## dcv_system_verification

Its parameters are passed through to [`dcv_verification`](#dcv_verification); set them on this rule's own entry.

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `agg` | `"max"` | choice | `"max"`, `"mean"` | CAMBER judgment: the critical zone should drive the reset |
| `stuck_std_ppm` | `5.0` | ppm (standard deviation of a zone's plausible CO2) | 1.0 to 30.0 | CAMBER judgment |
| `unoccupied_excess_ppm` | `300.0` | ppm (unoccupied zone CO2 median above outdoor) | 100.0 to 600.0 | CAMBER judgment |
| `assumed_outdoor_ppm` | `420.0` | ppm (CO2) | 380.0 to 500.0 | CAMBER judgment: roughly the present outdoor background, the same value camber.iaq assumes |

How to calibrate:

- `agg`: Keep 'max' when the sequence resets on the highest zone CO2 (critical-zone reset); use 'mean' when it resets on an average or on return-air CO2. *Note:* How the trusted zone CO2 series joined to one air handler are combined per timestamp. 'max' follows the worst trusted sensor.
- `stuck_std_ppm`: Look at the standard deviation of zone CO2 sensors known to be working over the dataset; set this well below the smallest. A sensor under it is excluded as flat. *Note:* Taken over the whole series of 250-5000 ppm samples, occupied or not.
- `unoccupied_excess_ppm`: Over nights and weekends a healthy zone CO2 decays toward outdoor. Take the unoccupied median minus outdoor on trusted sensors and set this well above it. *Note:* A zone is excluded as offset / miscalibrated when its unoccupied median exceeds outdoor by more than this (needs 24 unoccupied samples). Unoccupied hours come from the zone's OCCUPANCY point, else the delegated schedule.
- `assumed_outdoor_ppm`: Map an OUTDOOR_CO2 sensor if there is one; otherwise use the unoccupied overnight minimum of trusted zone sensors as a site estimate. *Note:* Used only when the zone frame has no OUTDOOR_CO2 point; only feeds the unoccupied-offset guard.

Fixed in code: a zone needs >= 24 CO2 samples to take part, and >= 24 unoccupied samples for the unoccupied CO2-offset guard, whatever min_samples says (camber/rules/ventilation_rule.py)

## dcv_verification

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `min_modulation` | `0.1` | fraction of the OA signal's p95 ((p95 - p5) / p95) | 0.02 to 0.5 | CAMBER judgment |
| `co2_setpoint` | `null` | ppm (CO2) | 600.0 to 1500.0 | CAMBER judgment: a site input with no default -- it is the BAS DCV setpoint |
| `occupied_only` | `true` | flag | `false`, `true` | CAMBER judgment: DCV is only responsible for OA while the space is occupied |
| `dcv_engage_ppm` | `null` | ppm (CO2) | 500.0 to 1200.0 | CAMBER judgment: DEFAULT_DCV_ENGAGE_PPM (800 ppm) when no setpoint is known |
| `min_demand_span` | `150.0` | ppm (CO2, p90 - p10 of the judged samples) | 50.0 to 400.0 | CAMBER judgment |
| `min_lift_ppm` | `50.0` | ppm (CO2 with OA raised minus CO2 with OA at its floor) | 20.0 to 200.0 | CAMBER judgment |
| `econ_high_limit_f` | `75.0` | °F (outdoor air temperature) | 55.0 to 80.0 | standard: ASHRAE 90.1 -- the top of its fixed dry-bulb high-limit range, as the code cites it (no section cited); chosen high so that more hours are excluded when unsure |
| `oa_floor_cfm` | `null` | cfm (outdoor airflow) | 0.0 to 50000.0 | standard: ASHRAE 62.1 §6.2.7 (dynamic reset: the area component Ra·Az; the code notes section numbering varies by edition) |
| `breach_fault_pct` | `10.0` | % of judged samples (occupied, fan on, not economizing, OA not closed) | 1.0 to 50.0 | CAMBER judgment |
| `below_floor_fault_pct` | `10.0` | % of occupied fan-on samples (before the economizer and closed-OA exclusions) | 1.0 to 50.0 | CAMBER judgment |
| `excess_warn_pct` | `50.0` | % of low-demand samples (CO2 at or below its p25 and below the engage level) | 10.0 to 90.0 | CAMBER judgment: DCV that holds OA above its floor at low demand saves no energy (the docs cite ASHRAE 90.1 §6.4.3.8 for why DCV exists, not for this value) |
| `min_samples` | `24` | count (judged samples) | 12 to 500 | CAMBER judgment: one day of hourly data |
| `start_hour` | `7` | hour of day (0-23) | 0 to 23 | CAMBER judgment: a typical weekday office schedule (07:00-18:00) |
| `end_hour` | `18` | hour of day (1-24) | 1 to 24 | CAMBER judgment: a typical weekday office schedule (07:00-18:00) |
| `occupied_days` | `[0, 1, 2, 3, 4]` | weekday numbers (Mon=0 ... Sun=6) | 0 to 6 | CAMBER judgment: a Monday-Friday schedule |
| `unventilated_co2_ppm` | `null` | ppm (CO2) | 800.0 to 2000.0 | CAMBER judgment: 1100 ppm, the ~700 ppm-above-outdoor level co2_ventilation uses |
| `unventilated_fault_hours` | `4.0` | h (total over the dataset) | 1.0 to 24.0 | CAMBER judgment: an outage is judged by duration, not share of the dataset |
| `full_outdoor_air` | `false` | flag | `false`, `true` | CAMBER judgment: a site fact, not a threshold (0.93, #37) |
| `stratify_hour` | `true` | flag | `false`, `true` | CAMBER judgment: a valve on a time clock and CO2 mixes the two in a pooled lift (0.93, #37) |

How to calibrate:

- `min_modulation`: On a unit with a known-fixed OA minimum, the robust range reported as `modulation` should sit below it; on one with working DCV, well above. Set it between the two. Damper position and cfm give different ranges, so tune per OA signal. *Note:* Below it, with demand in the DCV range, the verdict is 'static' (warn).
- `co2_setpoint`: Read it from the DCV sequence (the CO2 setpoint of the reset loop or the top of its proportional band). Do not fit it from the CO2 trend. *Note:* None: the CO2-above-setpoint-at-minimum-OA sub-check is not evaluated, the engage level falls back to 800 ppm, and unventilated_co2_ppm falls back to 1100 ppm. When set, the engage level defaults to co2_setpoint - 200.
- `occupied_only`: Leave it on. Turn it off only for a space occupied around the clock with no OCCUPANCY point, where the schedule would cut real occupied hours. *Note:* Off: every sample is judged (still only with the fan on and not economizing), and the unventilated-while-occupied check runs on all hours.
- `dcv_engage_ppm`: Set it to the CO2 at which the sequence starts raising OA: the bottom of the proportional band, or about the setpoint for an integral loop. *Note:* None: co2_setpoint - 200 when co2_setpoint is set, else 800 ppm. Too few judged samples at or above it gives 'insufficient' (demand_below_engage).
- `min_demand_span`: Look at `demand_span` on units whose zones clearly fill and empty; it should sit above this. Lower it for lightly occupied spaces only if you accept a noisier verdict. *Note:* Below it the verdict is 'insufficient' (no_demand_variation), never a fault.
- `min_lift_ppm`: On a unit with DCV verified by a functional test, `demand_lift` is the CO2 response; set this well under it and well above the lift of a unit with fixed OA. Calibrating it on the unit you are judging is circular. *Note:* Taken within the hour of day when stratify_hour is on and enough same-hour pairs exist.
- `econ_high_limit_f`: Set it to the high-limit setpoint in the economizer sequence. Better, map ECON_CMD so the economizer need not be inferred. *Note:* Used only without ECON_CMD: samples with OAT at or below it are treated as possibly economizing and excluded (unless the heating valve is above 5 %). CAMBER temperatures are °F; an OAT trended in °C excludes nearly every sample.
- `oa_floor_cfm`: Compute Ra·Az for the zones the unit serves from the design documents, or take the design minimum OA from the TAB report. For a multiple-zone system the true intake floor is higher than the sum of Ra·Az, so Ra·Az under-flags (the safe direction). *Note:* None: the below-floor and excess-at-low-demand sub-checks are not evaluated. A number or a mapping {equip: cfm}. Checked only on OA_AIRFLOW or AIRFLOW, not on a damper position or fan speed.
- `breach_fault_pct`: Raise it if short CO2 excursions at minimum OA are accepted by the sequence (e.g. a slow integral loop). Look at `co2_breach_at_min_pct` on a known-good period and set it above that. *Note:* Needs co2_setpoint; share of samples with CO2 above the setpoint while OA sits at its floor (oa_floor_cfm + 10 %, else within 5 % of its range above its p5).
- `below_floor_fault_pct`: Look at `below_floor_pct` on a known-good period; set this above it. Keep it low: OA below the 62.1 floor while occupied is an under-ventilation fault. *Note:* Needs oa_floor_cfm. A sample counts when OA is more than 10 % below the floor.
- `excess_warn_pct`: Check `excess_at_low_demand_pct` on a unit whose DCV is known to reach its floor when zones are lightly occupied, and set this above it. *Note:* Needs oa_floor_cfm. Only lifts an otherwise 'ok' verdict to 'warn'.
- `min_samples`: Raise it for short-interval data (e.g. 96 for a day of 15-minute samples) so the verdict rests on more than a few hours. *Note:* Also gates whether a fallback OA-signal segment gets its own line and whether the unventilated-while-occupied check runs.
- `start_hour`: Set it to the start of the building's occupied mode, read from the BAS schedule or from the hour the supply fan starts in a typical week of trends. Better still, map the OCCUPANCY point, which replaces the schedule. *Note:* Used only when the equipment frame carries no OCCUPANCY point: a trended OCCUPANCY point replaces the schedule (WARMUP / COOLDOWN are excluded either way). Ignored for the verdict with occupied_only=False. dcv_system_verification also uses it on each zone frame to find the unoccupied hours of its CO2-offset guard.
- `end_hour`: Set it to the end of occupied mode (exclusive), read from the BAS schedule or trends. *Note:* Used only when the equipment frame carries no OCCUPANCY point: a trended OCCUPANCY point replaces the schedule (WARMUP / COOLDOWN are excluded either way). Ignored for the verdict with occupied_only=False. dcv_system_verification also uses it on each zone frame to find the unoccupied hours of its CO2-offset guard.
- `occupied_days`: List the days the building runs occupied mode, e.g. [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5] for a Saturday schedule. *Note:* A list of integers; each must lie in the range. Used only when the equipment frame carries no OCCUPANCY point: a trended OCCUPANCY point replaces the schedule (WARMUP / COOLDOWN are excluded either way). Ignored for the verdict with occupied_only=False. dcv_system_verification also uses it on each zone frame to find the unoccupied hours of its CO2-offset guard.
- `unventilated_co2_ppm`: Set it to the CO2 level at which the space must be ventilated, typically the DCV setpoint. *Note:* None: co2_setpoint when set, else 1100 ppm. A sample counts when the space is occupied, CO2 is at or above it, and the fan is off or OA is at or below 2 % of its p95.
- `unventilated_fault_hours`: Set it to how long an occupied space may go without outdoor air before it is a fault; half a working day is a common tolerance. *Note:* Hours are the count of qualifying samples times the median sample step.
- `full_outdoor_air`: Set it True only for a 100 % outdoor-air unit (no return air, no economizer damper), from the mechanical schedule. *Note:* True: the supply AIRFLOW, then SUPPLY_FAN_SPEED, serve as the OA signal when OA flow and damper are absent, and no economizer exclusion applies.
- `stratify_hour`: Leave it on. Turn it off only to reproduce pre-0.93 pooled verdicts; the pooled lift is always reported as demand_lift_pooled. *Note:* Falls back to the pooled lift when the same-hour strata hold too few pairs (lift_basis).

Not thresholds: `min_corr` (deprecated since 0.82 and ignored (warns; removal in 1.0): the verdict no longer uses Pearson correlation -- use min_lift_ppm).

## dx_indoor_airflow

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `freeze_if_missing` | `true` | flag | `false`, `true` | CAMBER judgment: a first baseline-mode run freezes its fault-free period |
| `targets` | `null` | °F (a per-unit mapping) | 15.0 to 22.0 | public source: the installer's target temperature split for the unit |
| `tolerance_f` | `3.0` | °F (either side of the target split) | 1.5 to 5.0 | CAMBER judgment: ±3 °F; no source is cited |
| `warn_f` | `1.5` | °F (median split residual against the baseline) | 1.0 to 4.0 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade; characterized on nist-heatpump-fdd, where max(1.5 °F, 2σ) flagged 2 of 90 fault-free files |
| `fault_f` | `3.0` | °F (median split residual against the baseline) | 2.0 to 8.0 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade; characterized on nist-heatpump-fdd |
| `warn_sigma` | `2.0` | σ (standard deviations of the baseline residual) | 1.0 to 4.0 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade; characterized on nist-heatpump-fdd |
| `fault_sigma` | `4.0` | σ (standard deviations of the baseline residual) | 2.0 to 8.0 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade; characterized on nist-heatpump-fdd |
| `min_samples` | `10` | count (cooling-mode rows) | 5 to 200 | CAMBER judgment: the smallest sample whose median is worth reporting |
| `min_baseline_samples` | `30` | count (cooling-mode rows) | 20 to 1000 | CAMBER judgment: the minimum for the regression on outdoor and return air (shared _dxfit default) |
| `min_split_f` | `8.0` | °F (return minus supply air while cooling) | 5.0 to 12.0 | CAMBER judgment: a DX coil at rated airflow drops roughly 15-22 °F; the 8-28 °F band is wide on purpose (screening-grade) |
| `max_split_f` | `28.0` | °F (return minus supply air while cooling) | 24.0 to 35.0 | CAMBER judgment: a DX coil at rated airflow drops roughly 15-22 °F; the 8-28 °F band is wide on purpose (screening-grade) |

How to calibrate:

- `freeze_if_missing`: Leave True for a first run on a known-good period; set False once baselines are frozen so a later run cannot silently freeze a faulty period as the reference. *Note:* Baseline mode (analyze_periods) only. False with no stored baseline declines the unit.
- `targets`: Take the target split from a chart that uses the return wet bulb and dry bulb where you have one (a fixed number ignores latent load), or from commissioning measurements at rated airflow. Deriving it from the scored trend is circular. *Note:* None: no target, so only min_split_f / max_split_f apply (each a warn). Shape: {'temp_split_f': 20, 'tolerance_f': 3} for every unit, or {'RTU-*': {...}} keyed by fnmatch patterns on the equipment id. The range is for temp_split_f.
- `tolerance_f`: Widen it where the return humidity swings widely, since the fixed target ignores latent load; a per-unit 'tolerance_f' in targets overrides it. *Note:* Target mode only: warn at the tolerance, fault at twice it.
- `warn_f`: Score a held-out part of a known-good period against its frozen baseline and set the floor above its largest residual. *Note:* Baseline mode only: a warn needs |drift| >= max(warn_f, warn_sigma × σ). Airflow faults under about 15% sit inside the fault-free scatter.
- `fault_f`: Keep it about twice warn_f. *Note:* Baseline mode only.
- `warn_sigma`: Raise it if a held-out known-good period trips the warn, e.g. with no return dew point to absorb latent-load swings. *Note:* Baseline mode only.
- `fault_sigma`: Keep it about twice warn_sigma. *Note:* Baseline mode only.
- `min_samples`: Raise it for minute data, where 10 rows is a few minutes of running; with hourly or averaged test points keep it low. *Note:* Target mode: rows needed in the frame. Baseline mode: scoreable rows in the current period.
- `min_baseline_samples`: Make the fault-free period long enough to span the weather the unit will be scored in; raise this if the fitted slopes look unstable. *Note:* Baseline mode only.
- `min_split_f`: Only for units with no target: set a target split instead where one is known. *Note:* Limits mode only; below it is a warn read as high airflow or lost capacity (charge).
- `max_split_f`: Only for units with no target: set a target split instead where one is known. *Note:* Limits mode only; above it is a low-airflow warn.

Not thresholds: `store` (a frozen-baseline store handle (in-memory when omitted), not a threshold); `site` (the site id the frozen baseline is stored under, not a threshold); `run_id` (the run id recorded when a baseline is frozen, not a threshold).

## dx_refrigerant_charge

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `freeze_if_missing` | `true` | flag | `false`, `true` | CAMBER judgment: a first baseline-mode run freezes its fault-free period |
| `targets` | `null` | °F (a per-unit mapping) | 5.0 to 20.0 | public source: the unit's nameplate / installation-manual charging target |
| `tolerance_f` | `3.0` | °F (either side of the target) | 1.0 to 5.0 | public source: manufacturer charging instructions (the common ±3 °F on target subcooling, as the rule module cites) |
| `metric` | `"subcooling"` | choice | `"subcooling"`, `"superheat"` | CAMBER judgment: TXV / EEV units are charged by subcooling, fixed-orifice units by superheat |
| `warn_f` | `3.0` | °F (median residual against the baseline) | 1.5 to 6.0 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade; characterized on nist-heatpump-fdd, where max(3 °F, 1.5σ) caught 91% of charge-fault files at 8% of fault-free files |
| `fault_f` | `5.0` | °F (median residual against the baseline) | 3.0 to 10.0 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade; characterized on nist-heatpump-fdd |
| `warn_sigma` | `1.5` | σ (standard deviations of the baseline residual) | 1.0 to 4.0 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade; characterized on nist-heatpump-fdd |
| `fault_sigma` | `3.0` | σ (standard deviations of the baseline residual) | 2.0 to 6.0 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade; characterized on nist-heatpump-fdd |
| `min_samples` | `10` | count (cooling-mode rows) | 5 to 200 | CAMBER judgment: the smallest sample whose median is worth reporting |
| `min_baseline_samples` | `30` | count (cooling-mode rows) | 20 to 1000 | CAMBER judgment: the minimum for the regression on outdoor and return air (shared _dxfit default) |
| `min_subcooling_f` | `2.0` | °F | 0.0 to 5.0 | CAMBER judgment: below about 2 °F of subcooling a TXV is fed flash gas (screening-grade universal limit) |
| `max_subcooling_f` | `25.0` | °F | 15.0 to 35.0 | CAMBER judgment: no charging target sits near 25 °F (screening-grade universal limit) |

How to calibrate:

- `freeze_if_missing`: Leave True for a first run on a known-good period; set False once baselines are frozen so a later run cannot silently freeze a faulty period as the reference. *Note:* Baseline mode (analyze_periods) only. False with no stored baseline declines the unit.
- `targets`: Copy the target subcooling (and superheat, for corroboration) from the manufacturer's charging chart or nameplate, at the conditions the unit mostly runs in. Taking it from the trend you score is circular. *Note:* None: no target, so only min_subcooling_f / max_subcooling_f apply (each a warn), and metric='superheat' declines. Shape: {'subcooling_f': 10, 'superheat_f': 8, 'tolerance_f': 3} for every unit, or {'RTU-*': {...}} keyed by fnmatch patterns on the equipment id. The range is for subcooling_f.
- `tolerance_f`: Use the tolerance printed in the unit's charging instructions; a per-unit 'tolerance_f' in targets overrides it. *Note:* Target mode only: warn at the tolerance, fault at twice it.
- `metric`: Choose 'superheat' for a fixed-orifice (piston) unit, whose charging chart is by superheat; otherwise keep 'subcooling'.
- `warn_f`: Score a known-good period against its own frozen baseline (a held-out part of it, not the fitted rows) and set the floor above its largest residual. *Note:* Baseline mode only: a warn needs |drift| >= max(warn_f, warn_sigma × σ).
- `fault_f`: Keep it clear of warn_f; about the residual a 10-15% charge loss gives on the unit, if a charging test or chart tells you. *Note:* Baseline mode only: a fault needs |drift| >= max(fault_f, fault_sigma × σ).
- `warn_sigma`: Raise it if a held-out part of the fault-free period trips the warn; the °F floor governs a very steady baseline. *Note:* Baseline mode only.
- `fault_sigma`: Keep it about twice warn_sigma. *Note:* Baseline mode only.
- `min_samples`: Raise it for minute data, where 10 rows is a few minutes of running; with hourly or averaged test points keep it low. *Note:* Target mode: rows needed in the frame. Baseline mode: scoreable rows in the current period.
- `min_baseline_samples`: Make the fault-free period long enough to span the weather the unit will be scored in; raise this if the fitted slopes look unstable. *Note:* Baseline mode only.
- `min_subcooling_f`: Only for units with no target: set a target instead where the nameplate gives one. *Note:* Limits mode only (no target, metric='subcooling'); below it is a low-charge warn.
- `max_subcooling_f`: Only for units with no target; a unit with an unusually high design subcooling needs a target instead. *Note:* Limits mode only (no target, metric='subcooling'); above it is an overcharge warn.

Not thresholds: `store` (a frozen-baseline store handle (in-memory when omitted), not a threshold); `site` (the site id the frozen baseline is stored under, not a threshold); `run_id` (the run id recorded when a baseline is frozen, not a threshold).

## economizer_high_limit

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `high_limit_f` | `65.0` | °F | 55.0 to 80.0 | CAMBER judgment: a typical, not universal, fixed dry-bulb high limit (CA Title 24 sets it by climate zone) |
| `min_damper` | `0.25` | fraction (OA damper, 0-1) | 0.0 to 1.0 | CAMBER judgment |
| `min_oa_pct` | `null` | % of supply airflow (OA fraction) | 0.0 to 100.0 | CAMBER judgment: the design minimum is a building property |
| `oa_margin_pct` | `5.0` | % of supply airflow (percentage points) | 1.0 to 15.0 | CAMBER judgment: allows for temperature-balance noise |
| `warn_pct` | `10.0` | % of fan-on samples above the high limit | 2.0 to 30.0 | CAMBER judgment |
| `fault_pct` | `25.0` | % of fan-on samples above the high limit | 10.0 to 60.0 | CAMBER judgment |
| `denom_min_f` | `5.0` | °F | 2.0 to 15.0 | public source: PNNL Re-tuning Ch.5 (the same guard as camber/oafraction.py) |
| `assumed_min_oa_pct` | `20.0` | % of supply airflow (OA fraction) | 5.0 to 40.0 | CAMBER judgment: a generic design minimum |
| `conservative_min_oa_pct` | `50.0` | % of supply airflow (OA fraction) | 30.0 to 80.0 | CAMBER judgment: above the design minimum of any ordinary mixed-air unit |
| `differential` | `true` | flag | `false`, `true` | CAMBER judgment: many economizers use a differential dry-bulb changeover |
| `fan_gate` | `true` | flag | `false`, `true` | CAMBER judgment: with the fan stopped the air temperatures describe still air, not the unit at work |

How to calibrate:

- `high_limit_f`: Set it to the high-limit setpoint of the unit's economizer sequence or the energy code for its climate zone.
- `min_damper`: Set it to the minimum OA damper position of the sequence, or the damper position the unit holds on hot fan-on hours in a known-good period. Used only when no mixed/return air temperatures or airflows are trended. *Note:* A sample counts as not locked out above min_damper + 0.05.
- `min_oa_pct`: Take it from the ventilation design, or measure the OA fraction at minimum damper position on a known-good fan-on period. *Note:* None = unknown: excess is scored against conservative_min_oa_pct, and OA that is excess only against assumed_min_oa_pct is declined.
- `oa_margin_pct`: Set it to the spread of the OA fraction at minimum position on known-good hot hours (for example its interquartile range).
- `warn_pct`: Read not_locked_out_pct on units known to lock out correctly; set the warn level above their spread.
- `fault_pct`: Set it well above warn_pct. *Note:* Must be at or above warn_pct.
- `denom_min_f`: Raise it when OA fractions scatter on hours with OAT close to RAT (n_masked_small_delta_t shows how many samples it drops).
- `assumed_min_oa_pct`: Prefer setting min_oa_pct; change this only to move the generic minimum used in the declined-case caveat.
- `conservative_min_oa_pct`: Prefer setting min_oa_pct; lower it only for a portfolio whose design minimums are all known to be lower.
- `differential`: Set it from the sequence: false for a fixed dry-bulb high limit, true for a differential (outdoor vs return) changeover.
- `fan_gate`: Leave it on. Turn it off only when the fan signal is known to be wrong (stuck status, a speed point that reads 0 while running) and every trended sample is a running sample. *Note:* The fan is read from supply-fan status, else speed, else airflow; a unit with none of them is judged ungated and the finding says so (the fan_gate metric).

## filter_fouling

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `change_dp_inwc` | `1.0` | in. w.c. | 0.3 to 2.0 | CAMBER judgment: a common MERV-13 final-pressure-drop alarm (filter and fan dependent) |

How to calibrate:

- `change_dp_inwc`: Use the filter maker's recommended final resistance for the installed filter, or the differential pressure at which the site changes filters; filter_dp_median_inwc of a freshly changed filter gives the clean baseline. *Note:* Warn when the median is at or above it; fault at 1.5 times it (fixed in code).

## free_cooling_missed

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `high_limit_f` | `60.0` | °F | 45.0 to 75.0 | CAMBER judgment |
| `active` | `5.0` | % of valve stroke (cooling valve) | 1.0 to 20.0 | CAMBER judgment: a valve parked at a few percent is not mechanical cooling running |
| `warn_pct` | `10.0` | % of free-cooling samples | 2.0 to 30.0 | CAMBER judgment |
| `fault_pct` | `25.0` | % of free-cooling samples | 10.0 to 60.0 | CAMBER judgment |

How to calibrate:

- `high_limit_f`: Set it to the economizer high limit of the unit's sequence (or a few degrees below, so only clearly cool weather counts as free-cooling weather). *Note:* camber.freecooling.free_cooling_opportunity defaults to 65 °F; this rule to 60 °F.
- `active`: Set it just above the cooling-valve position seen with cooling off on a known-good period (its 95th percentile when the chiller or compressor is off).
- `warn_pct`: Read missed_pct on units whose economizers are known to work; set the warn level above their spread.
- `fault_pct`: Set it well above warn_pct. *Note:* Must be at or above warn_pct.

## g36_afdd

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `heating_coil` | `null` | flag | `false`, `true` | CAMBER judgment: a missing heating-valve point is read as no heating coil |
| `mat_sat_as_coil_temps` | `true` | flag | `false`, `true` | standard: ASHRAE Guideline 36-2021 §5.16.14 (MAT/SAT may stand in for the coil temperatures, depending on the AHU configuration) |
| `min_oa_pct` | `null` | % of supply airflow (OA fraction) | 0.0 to 100.0 | CAMBER judgment: the design minimum is a building property |
| `mode_delay_min` | `30.0` | min | 0.0 to 120.0 | standard: ASHRAE Guideline 36-2021 §5.16.14 (ModeDelay; verified against Addendum p) |
| `alarm_delay_min` | `30.0` | min | 0.0 to 120.0 | standard: ASHRAE Guideline 36-2021 §5.16.14 (AlarmDelay; verified against Addendum p) |
| `avg_window_min` | `5.0` | min | 1.0 to 30.0 | standard: ASHRAE Guideline 36-2021 §5.16.14 (five-minute rolling averages) |
| `econ_damper_open` | `80.0` | % of damper stroke (OA damper) | 50.0 to 100.0 | CAMBER judgment: separates G36 OS#3 (mechanical cooling on 100 % OA) from OS#4 |
| `valve_thr` | `5.0` | % of valve stroke | 0.0 to 15.0 | CAMBER judgment: a noise deadband for 'coil active' |
| `warn_pct` | `5.0` | % of an FC's applicable intervals | 1.0 to 30.0 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade severity, not from G36 (G36 alarms every confirmed fault) |
| `fault_pct` | `20.0` | % of an FC's applicable intervals | 5.0 to 60.0 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade severity, not from G36 |
| `min_applicable_hours` | `24.0` | h | 1.0 to 500.0 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade, not from G36 |

How to calibrate:

- `heating_coil`: Set it from the unit's schedule or drawings: true when the AHU has a heating coil whose valve is not trended (the rule then declines), false to ignore a mapped valve. *Note:* None = inferred from whether a heating-valve point is mapped.
- `mat_sat_as_coil_temps`: Leave it on for an AHU with no heating coil between the mixed- and supply-air sensors; turn it off when another component (a preheat coil, an energy wheel) sits between them.
- `min_oa_pct`: Take it from the design minimum OA over design airflow, or measure the OA fraction at minimum damper position on a known-good fan-on period. *Note:* None = FC6 is declined. G36 uses the active minimum-OA setpoint over actual airflow.
- `mode_delay_min`: Keep the G36 value; lengthen it only if trends show the unit still settling after a fan start or mode change beyond 30 minutes.
- `alarm_delay_min`: Keep the G36 value; it should be several sample intervals long so that a fault must persist across more than one sample.
- `avg_window_min`: Keep the G36 value; on trends coarser than 5 minutes the window holds a single sample.
- `econ_damper_open`: Set it just below the position the OA damper holds when the sequence calls for full economizer (its 5th percentile on such hours).
- `valve_thr`: Set it just above the valve command's reading when commanded closed (its 95th percentile on idle hours).
- `warn_pct`: Read each FC's pct on units known to be healthy; set the warn level above the spread. Tuning it on the unit under test is circular.
- `fault_pct`: Set it well above warn_pct. *Note:* Must be at or above warn_pct.
- `min_applicable_hours`: Raise it for long histories so that a rare operating state with a few hours of applicability cannot set the severity; each FC's applicable_hours shows its base.

## heatpump_defrost

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `max_reversals_per_day` | `24.0` | reversing-valve transitions per day | 12.0 to 96.0 | CAMBER judgment: defrost at most about once an hour in cold weather (the rule module's comment), so 24 a day is a generous ceiling |

How to calibrate:

- `max_reversals_per_day`: Read the defrost-control interval (time- or demand-based) from the unit's manual, or count the reversals per day in a known-good cold spell and set the ceiling above that. Each defrost counts two transitions (into cooling and back), so allow for that. *Note:* Warn at the ceiling, fault at twice it. Heating/cooling changeovers count too.

Fixed in code: warn at max_reversals_per_day or more; fault at twice it (the factor 2 is fixed in code)

## hp_capacity_shortfall

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `warn_outside_pct` | `10.0` | % of occupied samples with a mode and zone temperature (per side) | 2.0 to 30.0 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade (provisional, 0.93) |
| `fault_outside_pct` | `25.0` | % of occupied samples with a mode and zone temperature (per side) | 10.0 to 60.0 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade (provisional, 0.93) |
| `saturated_pct` | `70.0` | % of the out-of-band samples with the unit running in the needed mode | 50.0 to 95.0 | CAMBER judgment: mostly working while out of band reads as capacity, not control |
| `idle_pct` | `30.0` | % of the out-of-band samples with the unit running in the needed mode | 5.0 to 50.0 | CAMBER judgment: mostly idle while out of band reads as control, not capacity |
| `min_hours` | `4.0` | h (occupied hours out of band, per side) | 1.0 to 24.0 | CAMBER judgment: ignore a side with only a few hours out of band |
| `heat_sp_f` | `68.0` | °F | 60.0 to 74.0 | CAMBER judgment: a stated default comfort band (68-76 °F) |
| `cool_sp_f` | `76.0` | °F | 70.0 to 82.0 | CAMBER judgment: a stated default comfort band (68-76 °F) |
| `band_tol_f` | `1.0` | °F (past the setpoint) | 0.0 to 3.0 | CAMBER judgment: the zone must be clearly past a setpoint to count as outside the band |
| `heat_rise_f` | `15.0` | °F (discharge air above the zone) | 8.0 to 30.0 | CAMBER judgment: a water-to-air heat pump delivers about 85-105 °F air in heating against a ~70 °F room |
| `cool_drop_f` | `10.0` | °F (discharge air below the zone) | 5.0 to 20.0 | CAMBER judgment: a heat pump in cooling delivers about 52-60 °F air |

How to calibrate:

- `warn_outside_pct`: Check the share of occupied time out of band in a known-good season; set the warn above it.
- `fault_outside_pct`: Keep it well above warn_outside_pct. *Note:* A 'mixed' verdict (working_pct between idle_pct and saturated_pct) is capped at warn.
- `saturated_pct`: Lower it for units that cycle on a thermostat (they run part of every hour even when short of capacity). *Note:* At or above: a 'capacity' verdict. Must stay above idle_pct.
- `idle_pct`: Keep it well below saturated_pct. *Note:* At or below: a 'control' verdict.
- `min_hours`: Raise it for long trends so a single cold morning cannot trigger the rule.
- `heat_sp_f`: Set it to the site's occupied heating setpoint from the BAS or the thermostats; better, map the heat_sp point so the rule reads it. *Note:* Used only when no heat_sp point is mapped (the finding then carries a caveat).
- `cool_sp_f`: Set it to the site's occupied cooling setpoint; better, map the cool_sp point. *Note:* Used only when no cool_sp point is mapped (the finding then carries a caveat).
- `band_tol_f`: Set it to about the thermostat's deadband or the zone sensor's accuracy, whichever is larger.
- `heat_rise_f`: Look at a known-good week: the discharge-minus-zone difference while the unit heats clusters well above zero; set this below that cluster and above the fan-only rise. *Note:* Ignored when compressor status and the reversing-valve command are both mapped.
- `cool_drop_f`: Look at a known-good week: set it below the zone-minus-discharge difference seen while the unit cools and above the fan-only difference. *Note:* Ignored when compressor status and the reversing-valve command are both mapped.

| `fault_hours` | `10.0` | h (occupied hours in the wrong mode) | 2.0 to 100.0 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade (provisional, 0.93) |
| `warn_pct` | `2.0` | % of occupied running samples (heating or cooling) | 0.5 to 10.0 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade (provisional, 0.93) |
| `fault_pct` | `10.0` | % of occupied running samples (heating or cooling) | 5.0 to 50.0 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade (provisional, 0.93) |
| `heat_sp_f` | `68.0` | °F | 60.0 to 74.0 | CAMBER judgment: a stated default comfort band (68-76 °F) |
| `cool_sp_f` | `76.0` | °F | 70.0 to 82.0 | CAMBER judgment: a stated default comfort band (68-76 °F) |
| `band_tol_f` | `1.0` | °F (past the setpoint) | 0.0 to 3.0 | CAMBER judgment: the zone must be clearly past a setpoint to count as outside the band |

| `cool_drop_f` | `10.0` | °F (discharge air below the zone) | 5.0 to 20.0 | CAMBER judgment: a heat pump in cooling delivers about 52-60 °F air |

How to calibrate:

- `warn_hours`: Scale it with the length of the trend you score: a couple of hours over a month is noise, over a day it is not. *Note:* A warn needs both warn_hours and warn_pct.
- `fault_hours`: Scale it with the trend's length, as warn_hours. *Note:* A fault needs both fault_hours and fault_pct.
- `warn_pct`: Check a known-good period: brief wrong-mode samples at changeover set the floor.
- `fault_pct`: Keep it well above warn_pct.
- `heat_sp_f`: Set it to the site's occupied heating setpoint from the BAS or the thermostats; better, map the heat_sp point so the rule reads it. *Note:* Used only when no heat_sp point is mapped (the finding then carries a caveat).
- `cool_sp_f`: Set it to the site's occupied cooling setpoint; better, map the cool_sp point. *Note:* Used only when no cool_sp point is mapped (the finding then carries a caveat).
- `band_tol_f`: Set it to about the thermostat's deadband or the zone sensor's accuracy, whichever is larger.
- `heat_rise_f`: Look at a known-good week: the discharge-minus-zone difference while the unit heats clusters well above zero; set this below that cluster and above the fan-only rise. *Note:* Ignored when compressor status and the reversing-valve command are both mapped.
- `cool_drop_f`: Look at a known-good week: set it below the zone-minus-discharge difference seen while the unit cools and above the fan-only difference. *Note:* Ignored when compressor status and the reversing-valve command are both mapped.

## hp_room_imbalance

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `warn_fight_pct` | `2.0` | % of co-occupied samples (one unit heating while another cools) | 0.5 to 10.0 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade (provisional, 0.93) |
| `fault_fight_pct` | `10.0` | % of co-occupied samples (one unit heating while another cools) | 5.0 to 40.0 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade (provisional, 0.93) |
| `warn_duty_spread_pct` | `40.0` | percentage points (difference between the units' active shares) | 15.0 to 80.0 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade (provisional, 0.93) |
| `warn_sensor_spread_f` | `3.0` | °F (median spread between the room's zone sensors) | 1.0 to 6.0 | CAMBER judgment: one room's sensors should agree within a few degrees |
| `heat_sp_f` | `68.0` | °F | 60.0 to 74.0 | CAMBER judgment: a stated default comfort band (68-76 °F) |
| `cool_sp_f` | `76.0` | °F | 70.0 to 82.0 | CAMBER judgment: a stated default comfort band (68-76 °F) |
| `band_tol_f` | `1.0` | °F (past the setpoint) | 0.0 to 3.0 | CAMBER judgment: the zone must be clearly past a setpoint to count as outside the band |
| `heat_rise_f` | `15.0` | °F (discharge air above the zone) | 8.0 to 30.0 | CAMBER judgment: a water-to-air heat pump delivers about 85-105 °F air in heating against a ~70 °F room |
| `cool_drop_f` | `10.0` | °F (discharge air below the zone) | 5.0 to 20.0 | CAMBER judgment: a heat pump in cooling delivers about 52-60 °F air |

How to calibrate:

- `warn_fight_pct`: Check a known-good season: brief overlap at changeover sets the floor.
- `fault_fight_pct`: Keep it well above warn_fight_pct.
- `warn_duty_spread_pct`: Raise it where the units in a room are deliberately unequal (a lead unit plus a smaller helper). *Note:* Warn only.
- `warn_sensor_spread_f`: Set it from the sensors' accuracy plus the room's normal stratification, e.g. from a spot check with a reference thermometer. *Note:* Warn only.
- `heat_sp_f`: Set it to the site's occupied heating setpoint from the BAS or the thermostats; better, map the heat_sp point so the rule reads it. *Note:* Used only when no heat_sp point is mapped (the finding then carries a caveat).
- `cool_sp_f`: Set it to the site's occupied cooling setpoint; better, map the cool_sp point. *Note:* Used only when no cool_sp point is mapped (the finding then carries a caveat).
- `band_tol_f`: Set it to about the thermostat's deadband or the zone sensor's accuracy, whichever is larger.
- `heat_rise_f`: Look at a known-good week: the discharge-minus-zone difference while the unit heats clusters well above zero; set this below that cluster and above the fan-only rise. *Note:* Ignored when compressor status and the reversing-valve command are both mapped.
- `cool_drop_f`: Look at a known-good week: set it below the zone-minus-discharge difference seen while the unit cools and above the fan-only difference. *Note:* Ignored when compressor status and the reversing-valve command are both mapped.

Not thresholds: `rooms` (a structural mapping {room: [unit, ...]} that declares which units share a room (else the topology), not a threshold).

## hw_plant_deltat

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `design_deltaT_min_f` | `20.0` | °F | 5.0 to 40.0 | CAMBER judgment: a typical hot-water loop design delta-T; the code says to confirm it against the loop's own design |

How to calibrate:

- `design_deltaT_min_f`: Read the design supply-minus-return delta-T from the boiler or coil schedules and set this a little below it. A low-temperature (condensing) loop is often designed for a smaller delta-T than a 180 °F loop. *Note:* Severity is fixed in code: warn when >= 20 % of boiler-running hours sit below this, fault at >= 50 %.

## hw_pump_dp_reset

No tunable parameters.

Fixed in code: fault when the pump runs near full speed (>= 90 % speed) for >= 60 % of its running time; warn at >= 30 % near full, or near minimum (<= 25 % speed) for >= 50 %; running means speed > 5 %; a DP setpoint with a standard deviation under 0.5 (its own units) counts as flat (no reset); fixed in code (camber/rules/hwpump_rule.py, camber/chwpump.py), not yet a constructor parameter

## leaking_valve

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fan_heat_f` | `2.0` | °F | 0.5 to 4.0 | standard: ASHRAE Guideline 36-2021 §5.16.14 (ΔT_SF, Table 5.16.14.7 initial value) |
| `delta_thr_f` | `3.0` | °F | 1.0 to 6.0 | public source: PNNL Re-tuning Ch.5 with CAMBER judgment (a coil-side shift beyond noise) |
| `valve_closed_thr` | `5.0` | % of valve stroke | 0.0 to 15.0 | public source: PNNL Re-tuning Ch.5 with CAMBER judgment (a deadband) |
| `coil_sensor_fan_heat` | `false` | flag | `false`, `true` | CAMBER judgment: coil sensors sit upstream of a draw-through fan |

How to calibrate:

- `fan_heat_f`: Run a known-good period with both valves closed and the fan on; the median rise from mixed air to supply air is the fan heat. Record the run in a config comment.
- `delta_thr_f`: With both valves known tight, take the spread (e.g. 95th percentile) of the air shift beyond fan heat (median_delta_f and its per-coil values) and set the threshold above it.
- `valve_closed_thr`: Set it just above the position the valve commands read when the BAS commands them closed (their 95th percentile on off hours).
- `coil_sensor_fan_heat`: Set it from the unit's layout: true for a blow-through unit, where the fan sits ahead of the coils and the coil leaving-air sensors see its heat.

## night_weekend_setback

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `start_hour` | `7` | hour of day (0-23) | 0 to 23 | CAMBER judgment: a typical weekday office schedule (07:00-18:00) |
| `end_hour` | `18` | hour of day (1-24) | 1 to 24 | CAMBER judgment: a typical weekday office schedule (07:00-18:00) |
| `occupied_days` | `[0, 1, 2, 3, 4]` | weekday numbers (Mon=0 ... Sun=6) | 0 to 6 | CAMBER judgment: a Monday-Friday schedule |
| `min_unoccupied_run_pct` | `5.0` | % of unoccupied time | 0.0 to 20.0 | CAMBER judgment: a unit running less than this unoccupied is not missing its setback (#57) |
| `unoccupied_heat_sp_f` | `null` | °F | 45.0 to 68.0 | CAMBER judgment: no default; the unoccupied heating setpoint comes from data or config |
| `unoccupied_cool_sp_f` | `null` | °F | 78.0 to 95.0 | CAMBER judgment: no default; the unoccupied cooling setpoint comes from data or config |
| `min_setback_depth_f` | `3.0` | °F | 1.0 to 10.0 | CAMBER judgment: a held setback sits at least 3 °F from occupied comfort |
| `max_hold_duty_pct` | `90.0` | % of the unoccupied hours the fan runs | 50.0 to 100.0 | CAMBER judgment: a fan at or above 90 % duty in the hours it runs is running through, not cycling |

How to calibrate:

- `start_hour`: Set it to the start of the building's occupied mode, read from the BAS schedule or from the hour the supply fan or occupied-mode point switches on in a typical week of trends. *Note:* Used only when no occupancy point (the OCCUPANCY role) is mapped: one replaces the schedule.
- `end_hour`: Set it to the end of occupied mode (exclusive), read from the BAS schedule or trends. *Note:* Used only when no occupancy point (the OCCUPANCY role) is mapped: one replaces the schedule.
- `occupied_days`: List the days the building runs occupied mode, e.g. [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5] for a Saturday schedule. *Note:* A list of integers; each must lie in the range.
- `min_unoccupied_run_pct`: Read fan_run_unoccupied_pct on units you know are scheduled off; set the floor just above the scattered runtime they show (freeze protection, morning starts).
- `unoccupied_heat_sp_f`: Enter the unoccupied (setback) heating setpoint from the BAS program. *Note:* None means use HEAT_SP read in unoccupied hours; without either, the held-setback test compares the zone with its own occupied temperature.
- `unoccupied_cool_sp_f`: Enter the unoccupied (set-up) cooling setpoint from the BAS program. *Note:* None means use COOL_SP read in unoccupied hours; the cooling side of the held-setback test always needs a known unoccupied setpoint.
- `min_setback_depth_f`: Take the difference between the occupied and unoccupied setpoints in the BAS program and set this somewhat below it. *Note:* Also the minimum gap required between a known unoccupied setpoint and the occupied reference.
- `max_hold_duty_pct`: On a unit known to hold a setback, read its duty in the night hours it runs on the coldest nights; set this above that. *Note:* Needs sub-hourly fan status; a fan that runs whole hours never counts as cycling.

## outdoor_air_fraction

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `min_oa_pct` | `20.0` | % of supply airflow (OA fraction) | 0.0 to 100.0 | CAMBER judgment: a generic assumed design minimum; the real one is the unit's own |
| `cooling_cutoff_f` | `70.0` | °F | 55.0 to 80.0 | public source: PNNL Re-tuning Ch.5 with CAMBER judgment (camber/oafraction.py) |
| `denom_min_f` | `5.0` | °F | 2.0 to 15.0 | public source: PNNL Re-tuning Ch.5 (a stability guard on the temperature balance) |
| `fan_gate` | `true` | flag | `false`, `true` | CAMBER judgment: with the fan stopped the air temperatures describe still air, not the unit at work |
| `min_oa_pct_by_month` | `null` | % of supply airflow, per month | 0.0 to 100.0 | CAMBER judgment: only for a sequence with a seasonal minimum |

How to calibrate:

- `min_oa_pct`: Take it from the ventilation design or sequence, or measure the OA fraction at the unit's minimum damper position on a fan-on period with |OAT - RAT| of 10 °F or more; a 10 % minimum damper position can be a 1.6 % OA fraction. *Note:* Excess OA is OAF above min + 5 %; under-ventilation is a median OAF below min - 5 % (warn) or below half the minimum (fault).
- `cooling_cutoff_f`: Set it to the economizer high limit of the sequence: above it outdoor air is a cooling penalty, not free cooling.
- `denom_min_f`: Raise it when OA fractions scatter widely on mild days (n_masked_small_delta_t shows how many samples it drops); about 2-3 times the combined OAT/RAT sensor error.
- `fan_gate`: Leave it on. Turn it off only when the fan signal is known to be wrong (stuck status, a speed point that reads 0 while running) and every trended sample is a running sample. *Note:* The fan is read from supply-fan status, else speed, else airflow; a unit with none of them is judged ungated and the finding says so (the fan_gate metric).
- `min_oa_pct_by_month`: Enter the sequence's minimum for each month that differs from min_oa_pct, e.g. {6: 15, 7: 15, 8: 15}. *Note:* None = min_oa_pct all year. A {month (1-12): pct} mapping; each value must lie in the range.

## overcooling_min_flow

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `start_hour` | `7` | hour of day (0-23) | 0 to 23 | CAMBER judgment: a typical weekday office schedule (07:00-18:00) |
| `end_hour` | `18` | hour of day (1-24) | 1 to 24 | CAMBER judgment: a typical weekday office schedule (07:00-18:00) |
| `occupied_days` | `[0, 1, 2, 3, 4]` | weekday numbers (Mon=0 ... Sun=6) | 0 to 6 | CAMBER judgment: a Monday-Friday schedule |

How to calibrate:

- `start_hour`: Set it to the start of the building's occupied mode, read from the BAS schedule or from the hour the supply fan or occupied-mode point switches on in a typical week of trends. *Note:* Used only when no occupancy point (the OCCUPANCY role) is mapped: one replaces the schedule.
- `end_hour`: Set it to the end of occupied mode (exclusive), read from the BAS schedule or trends. *Note:* Used only when no occupancy point (the OCCUPANCY role) is mapped: one replaces the schedule.
- `occupied_days`: List the days the building runs occupied mode, e.g. [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5] for a Saturday schedule. *Note:* A list of integers; each must lie in the range.

## overcooling_severity

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tiers` | `null` | °F below the reference setpoint | 0.5 to 6.0 | CAMBER judgment: info 1 / warn 2 / fault 3 °F below the reference, described in code as Std-55-aligned (no section cited) |
| `window_min` | `60.0` | min | 15.0 to 240.0 | CAMBER judgment: an excursion must persist an hour to count |
| `relative_to_deadband` | `true` | flag | `false`, `true` | CAMBER judgment: a space inside the heating-cooling deadband is operating as designed |
| `start_hour` | `7` | hour of day (0-23) | 0 to 23 | CAMBER judgment: a typical weekday office schedule (07:00-18:00) |
| `end_hour` | `18` | hour of day (1-24) | 1 to 24 | CAMBER judgment: a typical weekday office schedule (07:00-18:00) |
| `occupied_days` | `[0, 1, 2, 3, 4]` | weekday numbers (Mon=0 ... Sun=6) | 0 to 6 | CAMBER judgment: a Monday-Friday schedule |
| `recovery_hours` | `2.0` | h | 0.0 to 4.0 | CAMBER judgment: morning recovery from setback is not overcooling |
| `reheat_saturated_pct` | `90.0` | % valve open | 75.0 to 100.0 | CAMBER judgment: a valve at or above 90 % is treated as fully open (heating maxed out) |

How to calibrate:

- `tiers`: Look at max_depth_f and median_depth_f on zones occupants do not complain about; set the warn tier above the depth those zones sustain. Calibrating on the zones you are scoring would hide a building-wide overcooling problem. *Note:* None uses the defaults {'info': 1.0, 'warn': 2.0, 'fault': 3.0}. A dict with all three keys, each a depth in °F, mildest first; the info tier is never counted as a fault.
- `window_min`: Lengthen it if short excursions (door openings, load swings) raise findings on zones that are comfortable in practice; keep it at or above the trend interval, since one sample at a coarser interval already satisfies it.
- `relative_to_deadband`: Leave it on when both setpoints are trended; turn it off only to measure depth below the cooling setpoint deliberately (it over-flags a healthy deadband). *Note:* With no heating setpoint the rule falls back to the cooling setpoint and caps the result at warn.
- `start_hour`: Set it to the start of the building's occupied mode, read from the BAS schedule or from the hour the supply fan or occupied-mode point switches on in a typical week of trends. *Note:* Used only when no occupancy point (the OCCUPANCY role) is mapped: one replaces the schedule.
- `end_hour`: Set it to the end of occupied mode (exclusive), read from the BAS schedule or trends. *Note:* Used only when no occupancy point (the OCCUPANCY role) is mapped: one replaces the schedule.
- `occupied_days`: List the days the building runs occupied mode, e.g. [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5] for a Saturday schedule. *Note:* A list of integers; each must lie in the range.
- `recovery_hours`: Measure how long zones take to reach setpoint after occupied mode starts on a cold morning (median across healthy zones) and use that. Used only when no WARMUP point is mapped.
- `reheat_saturated_pct`: Read the reheat valve command in known cold, fully-heating hours on healthy boxes; set this just below the level those valves actually reach (some controllers top out at 95-98 %, not 100 %). *Note:* Shared by overcooling_severity (sets these samples aside as a heating shortfall) and reheat_capacity_shortfall (reports them as its finding); keep the two equal.

## reheat_capacity_shortfall

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `heat_sp_f` | `null` | °F | 60.0 to 75.0 | CAMBER judgment: no default; the zone heating setpoint must come from data or config |
| `tol_f` | `1.5` | °F | 0.5 to 4.0 | CAMBER judgment: the unmet_setpoint_hours tolerance (1.5 °F) |
| `reheat_saturated_pct` | `90.0` | % valve open | 75.0 to 100.0 | CAMBER judgment: a valve at or above 90 % is treated as fully open (heating maxed out) |
| `warn_pct` | `5.0` | % of evaluated occupied samples | 1.0 to 20.0 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade, not a standard's (per the module docstring) |
| `fault_pct` | `20.0` | % of evaluated occupied samples | 5.0 to 60.0 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade, not a standard's (per the module docstring) |
| `min_hours` | `10.0` | h | 1.0 to 100.0 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade, not a standard's (per the module docstring) |
| `recovery_hours` | `2.0` | h | 0.0 to 4.0 | CAMBER judgment: warm-up after occupancy starts or a setpoint step-up is expected to run the valve wide open below setpoint |
| `start_hour` | `7` | hour of day (0-23) | 0 to 23 | CAMBER judgment: a typical weekday office schedule (07:00-18:00) |
| `end_hour` | `18` | hour of day (1-24) | 1 to 24 | CAMBER judgment: a typical weekday office schedule (07:00-18:00) |
| `occupied_days` | `[0, 1, 2, 3, 4]` | weekday numbers (Mon=0 ... Sun=6) | 0 to 6 | CAMBER judgment: a Monday-Friday schedule |

How to calibrate:

- `heat_sp_f`: Enter the zone heating setpoint from the BAS program or the sequence of operations; use a per-box mapping when boxes differ. *Note:* None means use the trended HEAT_SP; without it the rule declines. One value for every box, or a {equip: °F} mapping. A trended HEAT_SP always wins.
- `tol_f`: Set it above the normal control swing of healthy zones below their heating setpoint (a high percentile of setpoint minus zone temperature while heating). Keep it equal to unmet_setpoint_hours' tol_F.
- `reheat_saturated_pct`: Read the reheat valve command in known cold, fully-heating hours on healthy boxes; set this just below the level those valves actually reach (some controllers top out at 95-98 %, not 100 %). *Note:* Shared by overcooling_severity (sets these samples aside as a heating shortfall) and reheat_capacity_shortfall (reports them as its finding); keep the two equal.
- `warn_pct`: Compare shortfall_pct across boxes known to heat adequately; set warn above the highest of those. *Note:* Applies only once min_hours of shortfall have accumulated.
- `fault_pct`: Keep it well above warn_pct; raise it if seasonal design-day hours alone push healthy boxes past it. *Note:* Applies only once min_hours of shortfall have accumulated.
- `min_hours`: Raise it for long records so a few cold mornings cannot grade a box; lower it for a short test window. Compare with the finding's shortfall_hours.
- `recovery_hours`: Measure how long healthy boxes take to reach the heating setpoint after occupancy starts on a cold morning (median across boxes) and use that. *Note:* Applied after each occupied-period start and each heating-setpoint step up, in addition to trended WARMUP samples.
- `start_hour`: Set it to the start of the building's occupied mode, read from the BAS schedule or from the hour the supply fan or occupied-mode point switches on in a typical week of trends. *Note:* Used only when no occupancy point (the OCCUPANCY role) is mapped: one replaces the schedule.
- `end_hour`: Set it to the end of occupied mode (exclusive), read from the BAS schedule or trends. *Note:* Used only when no occupancy point (the OCCUPANCY role) is mapped: one replaces the schedule.
- `occupied_days`: List the days the building runs occupied mode, e.g. [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5] for a Saturday schedule. *Note:* A list of integers; each must lie in the range.

## reheat_minimization_g36

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `valve_thr` | `5.0` | % valve open | 1.0 to 20.0 | CAMBER judgment: the dual-max logic follows ASHRAE Guideline 36 §5.6.5; this value is not from G36 |
| `flow_margin` | `1.2` | - (multiple of the airflow setpoint) | 1.05 to 2.0 | CAMBER judgment: 20 % headroom over the minimum-flow setpoint before airflow counts as above minimum |

How to calibrate:

- `valve_thr`: Set it just above the valve command a closed valve reads in trends (leak-by or offset readings of a few percent), so that only real reheat counts. *Note:* The warn and fault levels (15 % and 40 % of reheating hours above minimum flow) are fixed in code.
- `flow_margin`: On healthy boxes at minimum flow, take the 95th percentile of airflow / airflow setpoint; set the margin just above it so sensor noise and tracking error do not count as violations.

Fixed in code: warn when >= 15 % and fault when >= 40 % of reheating hours run above minimum flow (camber/rules/reheat_min_rule.py)
