## sat_cohort_starvation

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cohort_frac` | `0.75` | fraction of the group's zones | 0.5 to 1.0 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade (provisional-untuned) |
| `sustained_frac` | `0.5` | fraction of active cycles | 0.2 to 0.9 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade (provisional-untuned) |
| `min_active_cycles` | `10` | count (request cycles) | 5 to 500 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade (provisional-untuned) |
| `min_zones_per_group` | `3` | count | 3 to 20 | CAMBER judgment: a common-mode pattern needs a cohort, not a pair |

How to calibrate:

- `cohort_frac`: On a healthy air handler at peak load, read the largest share of its zones requesting at once; set this above it.
- `sustained_frac`: Read group_sustained_frac on healthy air handlers over a hot week; set this above it. For SAT, corroborate with OAT: a hot design day can starve a healthy cohort.
- `min_active_cycles`: Raise it for long or fine-grained records; zones with fewer usable system-on cycles are reported unevaluable. *Note:* The cohort-starvation rules also need this many active cycles in a group before calling it starved.
- `min_zones_per_group`: Raise it so that a few zones requesting together are not read as a whole starved air handler.

Not thresholds: `groups` (explicit zone -> air-handler membership ({zone: ahu} or a callable), a structural input; None uses the served-by topology or a building-wide pool).

## sat_reset_effectiveness

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `min_cycles` | `12` | count (T&R cycles) | 6 to 500 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade (provisional-untuned) |
| `flat_frac` | `0.1` | fraction of the reset band | 0.02 to 0.3 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade (provisional-untuned) |
| `expected_move_frac` | `0.25` | fraction of the reset band | 0.1 to 0.8 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade (provisional-untuned) |
| `pinned_frac` | `0.15` | fraction of the reset band | 0.05 to 0.3 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade (provisional-untuned) |
| `mode_frac` | `0.6` | fraction of demand (or idle) cycles | 0.3 to 0.95 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade (provisional-untuned) |
| `min_mode_cycles` | `10` | count (T&R cycles) | 5 to 200 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade (provisional-untuned) |
| `wrong_dir_frac` | `0.5` | fraction of cycles T&R commanded a move | 0.3 to 0.9 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade (provisional-untuned) |

How to calibrate:

- `min_cycles`: Raise it for coarse trends; fewer usable rows than this and the rule declines.
- `flat_frac`: On a reset known to work, take the setpoint's range in a quiet period; keep flat_frac well below that range divided by the band. *Note:* stuck = actual range <= flat_frac x band while the expected range >= expected_move_frac x band.
- `expected_move_frac`: Keep it well above flat_frac so a flat setpoint is called stuck only when the requests clearly demanded movement.
- `pinned_frac`: Set it to cover the setpoint's normal jitter around an end of its range on a working reset.
- `mode_frac`: Read pct_unresponsive and pct_untrimmed on a reset known to work; set mode_frac above both.
- `min_mode_cycles`: Raise it on long records to judge the not-responding and not-trimming modes on more evidence.
- `wrong_dir_frac`: Raise it when a coarser trend cadence than the controller makes moves look reversed on a reset known to work.

## sat_rogue_zone_census

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dominance_frac` | `0.5` | fraction of active cycles | 0.2 to 0.9 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade (provisional-untuned) |
| `share_mult` | `2.0` | - (multiple of an equal share) | 1.2 to 5.0 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade (provisional-untuned) |
| `min_share` | `0.3` | fraction of the group's requests | 0.1 to 0.8 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade (provisional-untuned) |
| `min_active_cycles` | `10` | count (request cycles) | 5 to 500 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade (provisional-untuned) |
| `min_zones_per_group` | `2` | count | 2 to 20 | CAMBER judgment: a rogue needs at least one sibling to be compared with |

How to calibrate:

- `dominance_frac`: On a group with no known rogue, read the highest zone binding fraction; set this above it.
- `share_mult`: A rogue needs share >= max(min_share, share_mult / n_zones); raise it to demand a more lopsided share in groups with many zones.
- `min_share`: On a healthy group, read the largest zone share of requests; set this above it.
- `min_active_cycles`: Raise it for long or fine-grained records; zones with fewer usable system-on cycles are reported unevaluable. *Note:* The cohort-starvation rules also need this many active cycles in a group before calling it starved.
- `min_zones_per_group`: Raise it when small groups flag zones that merely serve a hotter space.

Not thresholds: `groups` (explicit zone -> air-handler membership ({zone: ahu} or a callable), a structural input; None uses the served-by topology or a building-wide pool).

## simultaneous_heat_cool

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dehumidification` | `null` | flag | `false`, `true` | CAMBER judgment: the unit's sequence is unknown until declared |
| `reheat_lift_f` | `2.0` | °F | 0.5 to 6.0 | CAMBER judgment: a supply-air rise over the cooling-coil leaving air beyond sensor noise means heat is added after the coil |
| `dewpoint_margin_f` | `2.0` | °F | 0.0 to 5.0 | CAMBER judgment: allows for sensor and dew-point approximation error |
| `humid_rh_pct` | `55.0` | % relative humidity (return air) | 40.0 to 70.0 | CAMBER judgment: a common upper bound of the comfort humidity band |
| `fault_pct` | `5.0` | % of occupied hours | 1.0 to 30.0 | CAMBER judgment |
| `warn_pct` | `1.0` | % of occupied hours | 0.1 to 10.0 | CAMBER judgment |

How to calibrate:

- `dehumidification`: Read the unit's sequence of operation: true if it has a dehumidification-with-reheat mode, false if it has none. Leave it unset only when the sequence is unknown. *Note:* None = unknown: each both-open interval is classified from the coil-leaving temperature, dew point and humidity. True accepts reheat after the coil as dehumidification unless a dew point shows the coil dry; False counts every both-open interval.
- `reheat_lift_f`: In a known dehumidification period, take the supply-air minus coil-leaving temperature; in a cooling-only period with the heating valve shut, the same difference (fan heat and sensor offset) sets the floor. Choose a value between the two.
- `dewpoint_margin_f`: Compare the coil-leaving temperature with the entering dew point on hours the coil is known to condense (drain-pan flow, a falling return humidity); widen the margin if those hours read as dry.
- `humid_rh_pct`: Set it to the unit's humidity setpoint or high-humidity limit from the sequence. Used only where no dew point can be formed.
- `fault_pct`: Look at simultaneous_hc_pct (unexplained_hc_pct when dehumidification is classified) on units known to be healthy; set the fault level well above their spread. Tuning it on the unit under test is circular. *Note:* Must be at or above warn_pct.
- `warn_pct`: Set it just above the both-open share that healthy units show during valve changeovers (read simultaneous_hc_pct on a known-good period).

## source_loop_deltat

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `design_deltat_f` | `10.0` | °F (loop return minus supply, magnitude) | 6.0 to 15.0 | public source: ASHRAE / IGSHPA closed-loop heat-pump design practice (about 8-12 °F at roughly 3 gpm per ton), as the rule module cites; not a standard requirement |
| `flat_deltat_f` | `1.0` | °F (loop return minus supply, magnitude) | 0.3 to 3.0 | CAMBER judgment: under 1 °F the loop carries next to no heat |
| `warn_flat_pct` | `50.0` | % of pumping samples | 20.0 to 80.0 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade (provisional, 0.93) |
| `fault_flat_pct` | `80.0` | % of pumping samples | 50.0 to 95.0 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade (provisional, 0.93) |
| `min_pump_speed_pct` | `5.0` | % of full pump speed | 0.0 to 30.0 | CAMBER judgment: any speed above a near-zero command counts as pumping |
| `min_hours` | `24.0` | h (pumping hours with both loop temperatures) | 6.0 to 168.0 | CAMBER judgment: at least a day of pumping |

How to calibrate:

- `design_deltat_f`: Use the loop's design ΔT from the mechanical schedules or the design flow and block load. *Note:* Warn needs the 90th-percentile |ΔT| below half of it; fault, below a quarter.
- `flat_deltat_f`: Set it a little above the combined error of the two loop sensors; check with the pumps running and every heat pump off, where |ΔT| should read near zero.
- `warn_flat_pct`: Check the flat share in a known-good season with a working DP reset; set the warn above it.
- `fault_flat_pct`: Keep it well above warn_flat_pct.
- `min_pump_speed_pct`: Set it just above the speed signal the drive reports when stopped. *Note:* Used only when no pump status is mapped.
- `min_hours`: Raise it to a week where the loop load swings with occupancy.

## supply_air_control

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tol_F` | `2.0` | °F | 0.5 to 5.0 | CAMBER judgment: the ±2 °F band a tuned discharge-air loop holds |
| `warn_pct` | `10.0` | % of fan-on running samples | 2.0 to 30.0 | CAMBER judgment |
| `fault_pct` | `25.0` | % of fan-on running samples | 10.0 to 60.0 | CAMBER judgment |

How to calibrate:

- `tol_F`: On a known-good period take the 95th percentile of |SAT - setpoint| over fan-on hours (mean_abs_dev_F is the finding's summary of it) and set the tolerance just above it.
- `warn_pct`: Read off_setpoint_pct on units known to control well and set the warn level above their spread; tuning it on the unit under test is circular.
- `fault_pct`: Set it well above warn_pct, at the off_setpoint_pct where comfort or reheat complaints begin at the site. *Note:* Must be at or above warn_pct.

## supply_air_reset

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fan_gate` | `true` | flag | `false`, `true` | CAMBER judgment: with the fan stopped the air temperatures describe still air, not the unit at work |

How to calibrate:

- `fan_gate`: Leave it on. Turn it off only when the fan signal is known to be wrong (stuck status, a speed point that reads 0 while running) and every trended sample is a running sample. *Note:* The fan is read from supply-fan status, else speed, else airflow; a unit with none of them is judged ungated and the finding says so (the fan_gate metric).

## supply_air_reset_compliance

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `min_clg_sat` | `55.0` | °F | 45.0 to 60.0 | standard: ASHRAE Guideline 36-2021 §5.16.2.2 (Min_ClgSAT of the OAT-based SAT reset) |
| `t_max` | `65.0` | °F | 55.0 to 70.0 | standard: ASHRAE Guideline 36-2021 §5.16.2.2 (the upper end of the OAT-based SAT reset) |
| `oat_min` | `60.0` | °F | 40.0 to 70.0 | standard: ASHRAE Guideline 36-2021 §5.16.2.2 (low end of the OAT reset band) |
| `oat_max` | `70.0` | °F | 55.0 to 85.0 | standard: ASHRAE Guideline 36-2021 §5.16.2.2 (high end of the OAT reset band) |
| `tol_f` | `1.0` | °F | 0.5 to 3.0 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade (docs/TR-RESET.md: provisional, untuned) |
| `warn_pct` | `40.0` | % of gated samples | 10.0 to 80.0 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade (docs/TR-RESET.md: provisional, untuned) |
| `warn_gap_f` | `2.0` | °F | 0.5 to 5.0 | CAMBER judgment: a trivially small persistent gap should not warn |
| `track_gap_f` | `5.0` | °F | 2.0 to 10.0 | CAMBER judgment: screening-grade (docs/TR-RESET.md) |
| `fan_gate` | `true` | flag | `false`, `true` | CAMBER judgment: with the fan stopped the air temperatures describe still air, not the unit at work |
| `occupied_only` | `true` | flag | `false`, `true` | CAMBER judgment: the reset applies in occupied mode |

How to calibrate:

- `min_clg_sat`: Set it to the unit's minimum cooling supply-air setpoint from its sequence or BAS program; a non-G36 value marks the map as configured (reset_source).
- `t_max`: Set it to the highest cooling supply-air setpoint the sequence allows (G36 resets it further by trim-and-respond; use the typical value if it varies). *Note:* Must be above min_clg_sat.
- `oat_min`: Set it to the outdoor temperature at or below which the sequence holds the warmest supply air. *Note:* Must be below oat_max. Samples at or above it are the warm-weather samples of the tracking check.
- `oat_max`: Set it to the outdoor temperature at or above which the sequence holds min_clg_sat.
- `tol_f`: Set it to the supply-air sensor's tolerance plus the loop's normal deadband; the mean_abs_error_f of a unit known to follow its reset shows the floor.
- `warn_pct`: Read pct_below_g36_target on units known to follow the reset and set the warn level above their spread; scoring the same units you tuned on is circular. *Note:* Also the share of warm-weather samples above target that trips the NOT-tracking warn.
- `warn_gap_f`: Set it to the smallest mean below-target gap worth a reheat fix -- roughly the supply air change that moves reheat energy noticeably at the site (mean_gap_f reports it).
- `track_gap_f`: Read mean_above_gap_f on units known to track their reset in warm weather; set it well above that.
- `fan_gate`: Leave it on. Turn it off only when the fan signal is known to be wrong (stuck status, a speed point that reads 0 while running) and every trended sample is a running sample. *Note:* The fan is read from supply-fan status, else speed, else airflow; a unit with none of them is judged ungated and the finding says so (the fan_gate metric).
- `occupied_only`: Leave it on. With no trended occupancy the gate assumes weekdays 07-18; map an occupancy point, or turn it off for a unit that runs occupied around the clock.

Not thresholds: `reset_source` (a provenance label printed in the finding, not a threshold).

## unmet_setpoint_hours

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tol_F` | `1.5` | °F | 0.5 to 4.0 | CAMBER judgment |
| `warn_pct` | `5.0` | % of occupied samples | 1.0 to 20.0 | CAMBER judgment |
| `fault_pct` | `15.0` | % of occupied samples | 5.0 to 50.0 | CAMBER judgment |
| `start_hour` | `7` | hour of day (0-23) | 0 to 23 | CAMBER judgment: a typical weekday office schedule (07:00-18:00) |
| `end_hour` | `18` | hour of day (1-24) | 1 to 24 | CAMBER judgment: a typical weekday office schedule (07:00-18:00) |

How to calibrate:

- `tol_F`: Set it above the normal control swing of healthy zones around their setpoints (a high percentile of the excursion beyond setpoint in comfortable hours). *Note:* Keep it equal to reheat_capacity_shortfall's tol_f.
- `warn_pct`: Compare unmet_pct across zones without comfort complaints; set warn above the highest of those.
- `fault_pct`: Keep it well above warn_pct; the rule counts a symptom, so raise it where design-day hours alone push healthy zones past it.
- `start_hour`: Set it to the start of the building's occupied mode, read from the BAS schedule or from the hour the supply fan or occupied-mode point switches on in a typical week of trends. *Note:* Used only when no occupancy point (the OCCUPANCY role) is mapped: one replaces the schedule.
- `end_hour`: Set it to the end of occupied mode (exclusive), read from the BAS schedule or trends. *Note:* Used only when no occupancy point (the OCCUPANCY role) is mapped: one replaces the schedule.

## zones_heat_cool_census

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `start_hour` | `7` | hour of day (0-23) | 0 to 23 | CAMBER judgment: a typical weekday office schedule (07:00-18:00) |
| `end_hour` | `18` | hour of day (1-24) | 1 to 24 | CAMBER judgment: a typical weekday office schedule (07:00-18:00) |
| `occupied_days` | `[0, 1, 2, 3, 4]` | weekday numbers (Mon=0 ... Sun=6) | 0 to 6 | CAMBER judgment: a Monday-Friday schedule |

How to calibrate:

- `start_hour`: Set it to the start of the building's occupied mode, read from the BAS schedule or from the hour the supply fan or occupied-mode point switches on in a typical week of trends. *Note:* Used only when no occupancy point (the OCCUPANCY role) is mapped: one replaces the schedule.
- `end_hour`: Set it to the end of occupied mode (exclusive), read from the BAS schedule or trends. *Note:* Used only when no occupancy point (the OCCUPANCY role) is mapped: one replaces the schedule.
- `occupied_days`: List the days the building runs occupied mode, e.g. [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5] for a Saturday schedule. *Note:* A list of integers; each must lie in the range.
